If you look at the map, those are in fact the areas of defence of our units. You have to bear in mind that there is an air field here. Let me see if it is on the map. Here it is. Furthermore, the main forces of the brigade were mainly to the north, to the east, and to the south of the town of Urosevac. None of these villages that you mentioned here is outside the combat disposition of the brigade. All of them are within the areas of deployment of the brigade. Most probably when they were taking up their positions this witness called it surrounding of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No. That's not witness testimony. That's an allegation from the indictment. It says: "During the period between the 24th of March and the 14th of April -" that period of 20 days - "the forces of the FRY and Serbia shelled and attacked villages in the Urosevac municipality," I enumerated the villages and you just showed them on the map. So tell me, were there any other units but yours?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only units of my brigade were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did the units from your brigade in this period from the 24th of March until the 14th of April shell or attack these villages?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Technically speaking and security-wise, it is an impossibility, because to the left and right of these villages there were positions of our units. If you take Biba or Staro Selo, it's west of Urosevac. You cannot shoot at units in Sovtovici, Pojatiste, or Muhadzer Prelez because they are our units, our positions. All of these were positions of our units. All the villages you enumerated from the indictment are located here, in this area. Look. All of them were positions taken up by our units, so we couldn't fire or shell ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say or, rather, it mentions Papaz and Sojevo. It says that you ordered the local population to leave the villages.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At no point did I have information that anyone from the army of Yugoslavia was ordering anyone to leave a village. That's absolutely certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There was nobody else there apart from this unit?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The unit?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Varos Selo is to the south of Urosevac, and there are about 40 per cent Serbs there and 60 per cent Albanians. The people who lived there when the aggression started left in large numbers. This unit that was there was to the north of Varos Selo, about a kilometre away. So there was no reason to enter the village. The unit was in front of Urosevac in the area of defence, and that's this red line you see here. The village of Varos is almost linked up to Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What can you say about the overall time period mentioned in paragraph 63(j) from the 24th of March to the 14th of April? Was there a single attack on a village? Was a single village shelled? Were the inhabitants of any village ordered to leave the village?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units in this area were the assault force of the brigade. They were not allowed to move at any point until the beginning of the land aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please answer with a yes or no: Was there any shelling?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at any point in time was there any shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was there any burning down of houses or expulsion of the population?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no expulsion of the population and no burning down of houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. General, you brought with you order 4/336 of the 24th of March, and that's in tab 19. Can you find it?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is quite a voluminous order. So is this the original order of the 26th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a copy of the original, but it bears my signature and it was filed by me in the brigade. The content is the content of the original order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We can see at the end that it was made in 15 copies and forwarded to all subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was this order drawn up in accordance with military rules? One refers to the enemy, paragraph 2 refers to the task, 3 to adjacent units, 4 the decision, then the tasks of the various units are set, 6 refers to support. Is this the order in which orders are drawn up according to the regulations?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Combat regulations prescribe the way in which an order is to be drawn up, and this order has been done exactly in compliance with these regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. At the beginning you mentioned that: "On the 24th of March, by carrying out airstrikes, NATO launched an aggression against the FRY. The following forces ..." and so on, and you were expecting the forces you listed here.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So what were you expecting to happen?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain to you, Mr. Milosevic, the tactical position of the brigade to show how this evaluation was made. It cannot be done by numbers alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The direction from Macedonia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: To what end is this evidence being led?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that you can see how and why this combat disposition was ordered covering a certain territory. The allegation in the indictment is that crimes were committed in the area. The general has just testified about each and every one of these allegations in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We don't see the relevance. Move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, this shows the purpose of the deployment. According to the allegation, the purpose was to expel the population. It was a joint criminal enterprise. It was to expel and kill the Albanians. However, this order shows that the purpose was to prevent ground forces assaulting the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have -- you and your witnesses have an obsession with formalism. It doesn't matter what the order says. What matters is what actually happened. Move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I will ask the general whether the order was fully complied with in all the brigade units.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In organisation, establishment, orders, everything was carried out. The units took up positions in a timely manner, organised defence, organised a fire system, expecting a NATO aggression from the direction of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please turn to page 2, where it says, "I have decided as follows." What does it say in the first line?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you should not examine on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will admit this order. We have it. We can read it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, but may I put just one question in connection with it, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Just one question, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in view of the fact that your decision was to organise defence, decisive defence in the assigned zone, does this kind of organisation of blocking defence and the deployment aimed at meeting aggression by ground forces, does it enable the units to carry out any other kinds of activities?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In brief, no. The brigade was on the first line of the defence of the corps. It was at the state border in the border belt. It was intended to protect the state. That's what blocking defence means, that there is no movement away from this line.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, as you said you would read this order, let me just draw your attention to page 7 where it says, among other things, that international law was to be fully complied with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You're trying to do indirectly what I told you not to do. Move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, your documents include an order by General Lazarevic of the 31st of March, and the sanitisation of the terrain is ordered by the units of the JNA in their areas of responsibility, and special units are to be set up to carry this out, according to decisions by the commanders, and it further goes on to talk about supplies. What can you say about this document? What does it refer to and can you comment on it very briefly?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the order of corps command of the 31st of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the corps commander. And this order defines the procedure to be carried out in connection with the dead, the wounded, both soldiers and civilians, as well as terrorists. Besides this, it describes what is to be done with the carcasses of animals, how they are to be removed from the ground, all with a view to protection of the units in the area, that is in the area of defence, the protection of the population and the humane treatment of people. This order assigns specific tasks and describes the equipment and materiel to be employed, starting with the investigating judge, doctors, veterinarians, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 4, it says: "Former hygiene and sanitation team per needs and at the decision of the commander of the company brigade."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it goes on to explain what a sanitation team consists of.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has to have an investigating judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We can read that order as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Robinson. Mr. Robinson, as we are now tendering documents, I omitted to tender the document I put on the ELMO to begin with. It's the one signed by Mr. Nice of the 26th of May, 2005, containing the information from their investigator about the 12 members of the KLA, as it says here, KLA soldiers in Kotlina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With respect to these orders, Mr. Robinson, please explain something to me.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that exhibit will be D331.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And with regard to some documents to which you referred and which were used but not tendered, we'll admit tabs 11, 13, 14, and 15. Yesterday [sic].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, please explain something to me. When you say you don't want to hear the contents of the orders, as far as I can understand, I am being prosecuted for command responsibility; therefore, the content of orders is very important. Either I am being prosecuted for command responsibility or you're saying that I personally went out onto the ground to kill someone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The orders are there. We can read them. We have admitted them. They are in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can read what it says in them, but the commander who actually wrote the orders can give pertinent explanations. Otherwise, it would not be necessary to consider any Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. documents here in the courtroom. But as you know, Mr. Nice went through all the documents he presented in great detail, or at least some of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in tab 21 there is an order written by you. This is not an order by your corps commander but an order written by you. Does it fully comply with the orders you received from your superiors?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is order that I issued. When the corps commander issues an order, then I issue my own order to my subordinates, and it goes on like that. It fully corresponds to what the corps commander ordered, except that in paragraph 4 I designate the unit and assign specific tasks for the sanitation. There's a squad commander, deputy commander, an investigating judge, a municipal public prosecutor, a rifle squad, a medical orderly, a veterinary medical orderly, two to four nurses, one to two veterinary nurses, one non-commissioned officer from the unit, and so on, and two trucks. So now specific tasks are assigned and the persons in charge are named. In this case it's Cedomir Cvetkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We have an order in tab 22. It's a very short order issued by you on the 4th of April 1999. And as far as I can see, but it's better if you explain it, it refers to measures for protection of the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "In the past few days, a number of instances of improper conduct on the part of the troops towards the civilian populations have been noted. The population in question is leaving the areas under threat from attacks by the Siptar terrorists and NATO airstrikes from the airspace. "In order to protect the population ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, please read a little bit more slowly because I see the transcript cannot keep up with you.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. "In order to protect the population leaving the areas under threat and to prevent any improper treatment of this population by individuals and units, I hereby issue the following order: "1. For all the population leaving the areas under threat, ensure free passage along the axes leading from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija towards the Republic of Albania and the Republic of Macedonia."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this refers to all the population leaving the areas, and in the beginning you said that they were leaving under threat from attacks by the Siptar terrorists and NATO airstrikes.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the population fleeing the NATO bombing and the Siptar terrorists is being given the possibility of taking refuge.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It goes on to say: "Exercise command to protect the population against improper conduct on the part of individuals and groups and ensure unimpeded passage of along their chosen route."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... an order that you made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And you referred to the population under threat from attacks by the Siptar terrorists and the NATO airstrikes. What is the precise evidence that you had to support that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where the NATO forces operated, and it was south-east and west of Urosevac. The air field was the constant target of NATO aggression, and we had a lot of positions there and decoys to protect the forces that were located in-depth. The villages such as Varos Selo, Nekodim, Stara Selo, Kamena Glava, Sojevo, Biba, Raka, those villages, and they are all in this area here, were under constant attack by the air force, almost daily, especially around the air field and Kamena Glava. The population from the surrounding villages, although the villages appear smaller here than they are in reality, they're much bigger, but when there are bombs falling 500 metres to a kilometre from their houses it is quite natural for the population to flee the area, and they flee in the direction where they consider they will be safer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the actual situation, the factual situation. On Nekodim, bombs falling on Nekodim, on Varos Selo, for example, on the air field. It is normal that the population fled from the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you or anyone in your command, under your command, speak to any of the villagers who were fleeing to ascertain why they were fleeing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commanders of the units in the field, locals reported to them straight away, asking to be allowed to leave in the direction they wanted to go. Some went to the northern stretches of Kosovo. Others went towards Macedonia, and the fewest from this area went towards Albania. They asked whether they could take shelter and preserve the lives of their women and children, not to have them killed in their houses. And I quoted the example of Doganovic where five children were killed, five children belonging to one family, and of course the families had to flee straight away. Not only that family but practically the whole village left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic, we'll admit that order. We can read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just on one matter. General, what gave rise to this order was that there were a number of instances of improper conduct on the part of troops towards the civilian population. Can you give me an example of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A specific example? Commanders of units who did not allow civilians to move around their area, their region, and prevented people from leaving. They were usually the commanders of platoons and companies. After consultations with the battalion commanders - and they consulted me in turn - I allowed what I allowed pursuant to this order and wrote an order out, saying what kind of conduct should be applied in the area under NATO airstrikes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you view what these commanders were doing as improper conduct and a threat towards the civilian population? It doesn't sound like that to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that wasn't a threat to the civilian population. It was care and attention for one's own men so as to prevent columns of tractors and so on, because it's usually done in an unorganised fashion, of groups of people moving around in the area that they are defending. So after being given permission, they allowed the population to pass through and carry on in the direction they had chosen to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's it? That's the only improper conduct you're referring to, and that gives rise to this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't improper conduct on the part of these individuals, because the people considered, and that is certain, that it was better that the population was where they were, because those young people thought that the NATO aggression would not enter into inhabited areas. However, after the bombings, it became clear that the population had to leave those areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So can I repeat my initial question: What are the instances of what you call improper conduct on the part of the troops? Can you give me an example of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A concrete example would be this: If somebody wants to leave an inhabited area, the command doesn't allow them to pass through the region of defence, considering that to be a threat to them. They would prevent them. But they then asked their superior officer, commanding officer for permission. Pursuant to my order, the commanding officer would give him permission, and that is why this order applied to all units and not to prevent the movement of the population, the moving out of the population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Jelic, none of that sounds to me like what any ordinary person would describe as improper conduct, but if that's all you can say, then I can take the matter no further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, you emphasise here in point 2 that -- you say: "Comply fully with the rules of international law of war and provisions of the Geneva Conventions in the treatment of the population." You write that on the 4th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you say anybody that violates international war law is duty-bound -- that their commanding officers are duty-bound to take steps against this kind of conduct and persons engaging in it.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in point 4, is that part of the explanation you gave to Mr. Bonomy a moment ago? You say: "Direct the population leaving the crisis areas in columns in motor vehicles and on foot take the routes leading towards the Republic of Albania and Macedonia and prohibit any improper treatment of those people."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the substance of my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean that the people could be allowed to move on?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, and not have them be a target.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you go on to say: "When bodies are found of persons who were killed in the area of responsibility, report this to the military investigative judge so that the cause of death can be ascertained and proper documentation drafted."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And asanacija, clearing up the terrain, is done according to the rules governing this subject matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Thank you, General. Now, in tab 23 we have another of your orders.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I'd like to tender tab 22, the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tab 23, there we have another order of yours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Tab 21 is also admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does this order relate to?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order which ensures the security regime in the area of responsibility in order to protect the units, public law and order of the civilian population. It says: "I hereby order." In my areas of responsibility: "Implement the security regime in your zones of responsibility in coordination with the forces of the Republic of Serbia MUP, Ministry of the Interior. The focus is to be on protecting the units and RMS, maintaining public order and protecting the civilian population. "2. Clear up the terrain --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, this is one that we'll just read. We'll admit it and we'll read it. So move to the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just one question with respect to this document, if I may, Mr. Robinson. I wanted to ask the witness this in concrete terms, since he issued this order: What does point 4 relate to with regard to providing assistance to the MUP organs in efforts to ensure the return and protection of displaced persons?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, since there were a large number of displaced persons in the area, depending on the individual cases where combat was taking place, we had to give assistance first of all to the military police, in coordination with the MUP, to ensure that that population should be channeled and directed to places which were designated for the civilian population, whether it was temporary putting up in the forests and later on in the facilities to protect them from the low temperatures and to give them every assistance in the form of food, medicines, and so on, medical aid and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you also say that strict measures should be taken against all persons who violate the security regime.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Strict measures to sanction the perpetrators, taking regular steps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask that this document be tendered into evidence, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, tab 24 is another of your orders which you issued to prevent persons leaving of their own accord. I'm not going to refer to the entire order which relates to all forms of crime, but I just want to ask you one thing: Volunteers were mentioned quite frequently. Now, in point 2 you say that measures with respect to the military conscripts and volunteers are the same as they are towards everyone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... because we have a find a more efficient way of dealing with them. Ms. Higgins?

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I can assist. There are a number of tabs which I can indicate which it seems to me cover the subjects of protection of civilians in the zone of responsibility, NATO bombing in the areas of the indictment, detection and prevention of crime in the ranks of the army, and a number of combat reports, all by General Jelic. Those tabs are 21 to 27 inclusive, 29 to 31 inclusive, 33, 34, 36 to 39 inclusive, 41, 42, 44, and 45, if that assists, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'll consult as to the most efficient way of dealing with it. Mr. Nice, can you say, what is your position on these?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: These are all documents, indeed some of the earlier ones that the Court wanted the accused to take swiftly, are all documents that might require quite some exploration by us, dependent, of course, to some degree on the first observations that the witness may make. So I'm entirely in the Court's hands, but taking them swiftly may nevertheless not save you altogether from having to consider them, and consideration of them, of course, will cut into the time that I have, but I'm entirely in the Court's hands. But certainly I expect one or two of the early ones in particular to be the subject of significant cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, in the light of that, Mr. Milosevic, deal with them but as expeditiously as you can.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in tab 25 we don't have a order; it is your own report. But not to get ahead of ourselves, tell me: It's your report, is it sent to the command of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to all our rules and regulations, we report along these lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, I'm bearing in mind that paragraph 2, the places are mentioned which we have quoted, in the area of Glavica, Varos Selo, Nekodim, and so on. Could you read out what you were reporting about on the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see that with the help of this map here. I'd like to draw your attention to the date, the 16th of April, 1999, at around 800 hours, above Kisela Voda, it says here a village but in fact it is south or, rather, between Kacanik and Djeneral Jankovic. Halfway between the two there's a small water source called Kisela Voda where leaflets were dropped above the village. A large number of refugees is arriving from the Republic of Macedonia by train and bus and on tractors at the border and returning in the direction of Kacanik, which means they've crossed the border. On that same day, the 16th of April, that is, between 14.15 hours to 14.45 hours NATO aircraft were active in the sector Glavica, Varos Selo, and Nekodim, which is all below Urosevac. That's it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, from this can I see and deduce that they are bombing parts and villages in which the Albanians are returning from the border; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were persons who had fled for a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But were they already in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were in Macedonia, and they're returning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean they're crossing the border again and coming in?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And when they reached the vicinity of their villages, the aircraft launched airstrikes again with eight projectiles, plus two, which means a total of 10 projectiles in Nekodim, Varos Selo - that's this deployment area here - and this entire region that they were returning back from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you establish a link between that; they're coming back now and then they're being bombed?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see quite clearly who is expelling the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mean who isn't allowing them to return?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, who isn't allowing them to return. If you look at the hours, it is 0800 hours to begin with, and then 1400 hours, which means the people had left their villages, crossed the border, and then were coming back. And they were being bombed again, and what was left, they had to flee to Macedonia and take to the forests again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So what it says here at 0800 hours, they have crossed the border and had come back and were moving towards their own homes, and they were being bombed from 1415 hours to 1445 hours. The NATO airstrikes were bombing them.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the ten projectiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: To the three villages they were going back to, right?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is this a contemporaneous document from those times, General?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We won't dwell on that, then.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender it into evidence now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Tabs 24 and 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We have here another of your orders in tab 26. Is it indeed your order and your signature?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's the -- an original document, is it?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, original document, dated the 17th of April, 1999, and it relates to ensuring safety of the civilian population and cooperation with the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say: "Because of the NATO airstrikes and the attacks by the remaining Siptar terrorist forces on civilian targets, the civilian population in the brigade zone is daily exposed to direct attacks, putting their safety at extreme risk."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it comes after the situation we've just been analysing. That's the new situation. It says: "In order to prevent and reduce losses among the civilian population caused by the aggressor's attacks, I hereby issue the following order."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. So you're referring to reducing the losses among the civilian population, "I hereby order ..."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "I hereby order: "1. Form special forces - elements of combat disposition in all units, tasked with taking care of the civilian population." And the task is as follows: "In cooperation with MUP forces and civilian defence, promptly notify the civilian population about the attacks by the NATO aggressors and the Siptar terrorist forces, assist in providing shelter and evacuation, ensure the best possible conditions for the disposition and accommodation of the civilian population, assist in bringing in supplies, organising economic activities and in particular health care, maintain full public law and order, protect personal property and ensure personal safety, prevent any restrictions to the rights and liberties of citizens, except if their exercise poses a threat ... to the safety of the unit."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then you go on to say: "In sectors where the units are deployed, ensure full cooperation ... with the authorities ..." And you also say, paragraph 2: "Select, if possible, representatives-commissioners among the civilian population ..."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in order to organise better organisation of accommodation and care. Of course, regardless of the fact that we provided security and guidance, sometimes people were not able to move on primarily for security reasons; their own security and that of the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What else do you say in this order?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Treat the population humanely. That's paragraph 5: "In all other matters related to the treatment of the civilian population, act in an extremely humane and responsible way in accordance with all the VJ rules and provisions of international humanitarian law." So that's in line with the orders above.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's in cases where their safety is endangered in a dramatic way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I would like to tender this as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 26, the order of General Jelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 27, we find your regular combat report that you sent on the 19th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We will not dwell on it for long. Let's just look at the beginning when you discuss the enemy. You say in the broader area of deployment of the armoured battalion - that was Kamena Glava - from the VAP --

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is airspace.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: -- NATO aircraft attacked the agricultural air field sector "in five raids, with two to four missiles and cluster bombs." You go on to say that in the area of Kurdi Mahala a Motorola hand-held radio was found in one of the Siptar houses.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was found by the military police. And in the village of Slivovo, two bodies of Siptar terrorists were found and they were removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How were those two terrorists killed?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those two terrorists in Slivovo, which is here, in this area facing Stimlje, they went into the combat deployment of the brigade armed and opened fire on the soldiers. The soldiers who were on duty returned fire and destroyed, that is, killed those two members of the terrorist group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In that incident, were there any more terrorists involved apart from the two?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These two who came closer to the combat deployment of the unit were killed. Others who were further away in the woods fled. I don't know if any of them were injured or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender tab 27 as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 28, General, there is another order of yours.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It has to do with establishing control of the territory and measures to secure troops and units. Describe it briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I ordered that everybody should use all their establishment resources in cooperation with the MUP authorities to establish full control, meaning that neither military personnel -- in the areas of defence, neither military personnel or civilians are able to move or allowed to move, primarily for reasons of their own security and the security of the units. Also, in one of the points I say as far, as the civilian population is concerned, always adhere to the previously issued order. By all available means prevent any threat to the security of the civilian population or their property. Paragraph 6: "Deal with the volunteers -" who are integrated in the unit, that means - "who are unable to carry out the tasks assigned to them, in the following manner: Establish if anyone is responsible for failure to perform the tasks or for other unlawful acts, and following that, return them by organised military transport to the command of the Nis military district." So do not leave anything to chance. "Prior to that, take disciplinary measures against persons responsible for possible criminal and other unlawful acts."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I just ask one question. There were actually volunteers in your unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those were soldiers, volunteers. But once they joined the unit, there are no longer any volunteers. It is in terms of the way in which they reported for duty; that they were people who had no wartime assignment but came to the army, were sent for training in the Nis garrison, and according to their military registered speciality, they would be assigned to various units, and the units would be reinforced with them. As soon as they joined the unit, they would be entered in the list of personnel, and they would be the same kind of soldiers with the same duties and responsibilities as any other soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, in the beginning of this document you said that the personal appearance of the unit members, especially the reserve forces, is not in compliance with what is prescribed, and it tarnishes the reputation of the Yugoslav army, and there have been instances of criminal activity. Could you give us some examples?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. It's impossible. We didn't allow any differences to exist within a unit between an 18-year-old soldier and a soldier who was 50 years old. Everybody had to be placed under command with certain prescribed obligations. Proper personal appearance, meaning short haircut, shaven face, adequate uniform with all the insignia of the state army, and as such the soldier would be placed under the command of his unit, be it a company, platoon, battery, whatever. And regardless of the way in which he joined the unit, what his motivation was, whether he was mobilised or volunteered, no difference was allowed between one soldier and another, and they were subject to the same legal provisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I asked you to give us some examples of criminal activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There have always been and there always will be, in a mass of 6 or 7.000 individuals, people who would engage in petty criminal activity; from petty theft attempts to take the goods home during the weekend, smuggling, et cetera, because mobilisation implies that you mobilise people who are normally civilians, who before joining the army were engaged in all sorts of activities. And in that mass of people, it is quite natural for these glitches to happen, those irregularities. People who probably behaved like that in civilian life as well and tried to continue in the same way once they joined the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, Mr. Kwon asked you if you had an example.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can remember a military conscript who stole, somewhere near the Dulje pass, a motor vehicle and some jewellery and tried to carry that to the interior of Serbia. He was caught by the MUP. I don't know what the outcome of his prosecution was, but I am more than certain that he was convicted. We can probably ask for information from the judiciary to see what sentence he got.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was there anyone in your brigade who was responsible for -- I'm not talking about theft now, who was responsible for murder?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody was ever brought before an investigative judge -- investigating judge in my unit, and nobody was prosecuted. Looking a year back from the said period, there was no one responsible for a serious crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you had no such examples in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until a year ago. Until a year ago, there was no such case. If a thing like that had ever happened, I would certainly be informed, and it would have been reported to the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General, I don't see from this document to whom this order was directed. Can you help us with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the right-hand corner, it says, "To the command." One copy is supposed to stay with the command, and the rest of the copies are handed out to subordinated units. It is the usual list of addressees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So in point 5 you ordered your subordinate unit to keep a precise war diary about everything. So every unit was keeping its own war diary?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. Every unit of the rank of a battalion or an artillery battalion had its war diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, with regard to this question by Mr. Kwon, in the right-hand corner we see, "To the command of," and then an empty space. In one of the orders we looked at previously, there were 15 units listed. What is this supposed to be filled in with?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can write "Command of the 3rd Mechanised Battalion," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So every unit within your brigade receives a copy of this order?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every unit subordinate to me, which is of the rank of battalion or artillery battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. In tab --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In fact, Mr. Robinson, can I turn to this now, this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In tab 29, you have another order, dated the 22nd of April. Is this also an original document?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can we stay with it for a while. I want some explanations. It says: "In the last few days, several members of the corps have gone missing or lost their lives due to the indiscipline of individuals in certain units of the corps." So you are referring to incidents within the corps. Did something like that happen in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in my brigade. We were simply informed -- or, rather, we received intelligence to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean that when incidents happen the entire corps is informed, even if it didn't happen in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be more precise to say that an order is issued to help prevent similar incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 4, what did you list here?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says -- in fact, this refers to the chief of security. He, as the authority in charge, is instructed to take all the necessary measures, in cooperation with the MUP, to prevent all form of criminal acts, and in parentheses, looting, removal of private property, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you go on to say: "Inform all members of the unit ..."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. "Inform all members of the unit and point out to them the damaging effects of all criminal acts on the reputation and morale of the unit members."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this order too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Tabs 28 and 29 are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tab 30, there's another order signed by you.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You note, first of all, that, "In view of NATO airstrikes and occasional operations of the Siptar terrorist forces, there have been considerable movements of the civilian population in the brigade zone of responsibility."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That was the 23rd of April. "In view of NATO airstrikes and occasional operations of the terrorist forces ..." And what did you order?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I ordered: "At the level of the battalion, artillery battalion, and the military territorial detachment, to assess the overall situation concerning the accommodation and movements of the civilian population. Wherever possible, protect the civilian population and prevent any movements or overspill. "In case civilians should find themselves in a combat zone, or if they are threatened by the operations of the NATO aggressor and the Siptar terrorist forces, evacuate them to the most suitable sectors and protect them from fire." Then I ordered the units to find the most suitable locations, such as villages, residential buildings and other facilities which are best suited for the evacuation and temporary accommodation of civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... raise in relation to an order of this kind?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Quite possibly not with this one I think. I mean, there are some general questions about all these documents, not least, for example, the point His Honour Judge Kwon raised, which is again manifest on this document and may be a general point, but apart from that, not this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think -- move on, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, it's not clear to me whether you're adapting the way I'm presenting my evidence to the way in which Mr. Nice is going to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I am determining the relevance. That's my job. It's relevant, but there's no need to go through it in detail. We can read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is concerned --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Judge Kwon is speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is concerned with the time you're spending to introduce these kind of exhibits. Speaking for myself, there can be a way to deal with it more swiftly. For example, as a group, emphasising some important points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you able to identify the essential elements of the remaining orders?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am only identifying the essential elements. But when you say that you're establishing the relevance, I have nothing against that, Mr. Robinson. However, I see that the basis on which you are determining the relevance is whether Mr. Nice is going to cross-examine or not. If he's not going to cross-examine, then it's not relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... point on it. It means that he accepts it and there's no need to waste time. Let us take up Judge Kwon's suggestion. If you can identify the essential elements of the remaining orders, then we can do that. Just put them to the witness and you'll get a yes or no answer and then we can move on. Consider that during the break. We will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to draw your attention to paragraph 19, because that's directly related to the orders that we have here and through which we are now moving. In paragraph 19, it says: "Slobodan Milosevic -" and then other names are mentioned - "while holding positions of superior authority, are individually criminally responsible for the acts or omissions of their subordinates pursuant to Article 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. A superior is responsible for the criminal acts of his subordinates if he knew or had reason to know that his subordinates were about to commit such acts or had done so and the superior failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or to punish the perpetrators." What I am just presenting is an accumulation of evidence to show that everything was undertaken to prevent any kind of criminal acts from being committed and to protect the population, and this is seen from the Supreme Command, the corps command, right down to brigade command level. The chain of command shows that. So the chain of command is equal to the chain of care and attention -- links in the chain of care and attention paid to the civilian population to prevent any possible detriment to the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I'm not preventing you from leading the evidence, it's the time that is spent on it. It can be dealt with more quickly. I have not prevented you from leading it, particularly in light of Mr. Nice's comment that there are matters that he will raise in relation to some of these orders, but let us move as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hesitate to take a minute, but it may assist the accused if the accused was to understand what professional lawyers, taking advantage of the procedures of the Tribunal would be, in served statements setting out the both provenance and significance of the documents, and it would then be open to the Prosecution to say, as to provenance, no challenge; as to significance, the following in their cross-examination. And that's the way that time is saved. If the accused, who I notice isn't attending necessarily to what I'm saying, takes the advantage of discussing matters with Ms. Higgins, he'll learn how time can be saved and better spent in court without losing evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Milosevic. Tab 30 is to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May tab 31 be admitted as well, not to have to dwell on that, because that is an order referring to the civilian population as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We now have a few of the tabs that I introduced later on. I hope you have them. They were presented before the witness started to testify. It is 31.1, and 31.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, do you have those documents, 31.1 and 31.2?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't have those.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll place them on the overhead projector, because I received them subsequently, a few days before the general started testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let them be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, would you place your copy on the overhead projector. I need my copy to be able to ask my questions. This relates to March 1999, and it is an act of the command of the 3rd Army, a team for liaising with the missions, a daily report. May we take a look at the second page.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it the 2nd of March or the 3rd of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is dated the 2nd of March. What does it say in paragraph 2 on the second page? The liaison officer of the 243rd Motorised Brigade. That is your own brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: A little slower, please. Could the speakers be asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic and the general, the interpreters are asking you to speak more slowly. Please observe the pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says the liaison officer of the 243rd Mechanised Brigade held a plan meeting with the members of the OSCE mission at 0900 hours. The meeting was attended by a representative from Prizren as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, skip a paragraph, because it says they controlled some numbers of the mechanised units. Now, what does it say in the following paragraph?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 1000 hours to 1030 hours a meeting was held with the leader of the team, Colonel Kotur, and a representative of the OSCE mission, Richard Ciaglinski, at his request and with respect to events in the Kacanik area, region. It was explained that they were activities on the part of the security organs providing security to the state borders in coordination with the forces of the 243rd Mechanised Brigade engaged in providing in-depth security. The representative of the mission agreed that such activities in the border belt were necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That means that the verifying mission verified your activities?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, this next document, to be found at tab 31.1, which relates to a report by the commander of the 3rd Army with respect to the missions, and the date is the 29th of October there.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the 26th of October, the following units were returned to their original garrison," and then the combat groups are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says on the 29th the army pulled out surplus equipment and manpower from the 243rd Brigade, which deviated from the structure established, and it says --

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says reduced to three tanks, 355 and ten BVPs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was that in compliance with the agreement?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was. There were certain differences, deviations, and then the agreed upon levels were arrived at.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, as we discussed your presence in the area of Dulje, Stimlje, in the vicinity of Racak itself, what does it say here under point 3? On the 27th of October, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From 820 to 920 hours in the barracks of Car Uros in the Urosevac garrison, a diplomatic military mission spent time and they were composed of the following members.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You needn't read out all the members. It says the team visited what, toured what?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The team toured the regions of the previous deployment of the motorised company, the -- of the 243rd Brigade, in brackets, Stimlje, Dulje and Birac. The mission did not have any comments or remarks to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So what you're saying is they toured those positions of that mechanised company in the area of Stimlje, Dulje, and Birac.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, covering the three points.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And at Stimlje is where your unit was. So that's that same company, is it, pursuant to an agreement?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And they had nothing to remark, no special comments to make?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now on page 2, what does it say there? And it says that on that same day, from 1145 to 1900 hours, in the same barracks we can see that there were representatives from the USA, Canada, and Tom Crosland from Great Britain, after a brief talk to the commander of the 243rd Brigade, they toured the composition in the region of Stimlje, Dulje, Birac, Doganovici and Gunca [phoen]. And the team was accompanied by Major Vidovic from the 243rd Brigade. The mission once again made no special comments or remarks.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That says that there was no deviation as to numbers. The strength of our units were as had been agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. So that is a contemporaneous document and relates to the mechanised company.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... concerned about these two documents and gone back to see how they were introduced, and they were introduced on page 78 at line 6 with a suggestion of what they were, and they're now being summarised as a suggestion of what they were. They haven't been provided to us in advance. It might help if the witness was asked in neutral terms if he's seen them before and if he knows what they are and what they relate to rather than being told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you familiar with these documents, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, from the reports sent from the army command and the actual state of affairs when the verifiers came to see us, for the most part these documents are known to me. Perhaps some of the details and the times is something that I am not fully aware of, but in principle we did not deviate from a single one of these documents from what we had agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How had they become known to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These documents. From these documents -- in fact, we wrote reports, my liaison officer, who was with the OSCE or, rather, on behalf of the brigade command, every report he wrote to the superior command he would inform me of one copy and put it on the records of the brigade. So I'm talking about my units, my areas, and not others. I can't speak about others because I'm -- haven't been kept abreast of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at document 31.2 now, dated the 3rd of March, 1999. That, too, is a daily report. I'm just going to look at the second page of that report. Do you have that second page?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it say there?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 2nd of March, between 0915 hours and 0950 hours, a meeting was held between the liaison officer of the Urosevac garrison and representatives of the OSCE mission in the club of the army of Yugoslavia in Urosevac. The representative of the mission, OSCE mission, from RC Prizren asked a question. He said When was it possible to hold a meeting -- when would it be possible to hold a meeting with the brigade commander at the Dulje junction -- pass, to discuss general security in the said region? The answer given was that a meeting would be held when the commander is available. On that same day, from 1000 hours to 1040 hours, a meeting was held between the liaison officer of the 57th Border Battalion - that is in my area of responsibility - with representatives of the OSCE mission. The mission representatives expressed satisfaction over the change in attitude towards them by the organs of the army of Yugoslavia. They stressed that the problem had been solved of approaching the border belt and asked a map -- be given a map with the border belt marked in of a radius of five kilometres for them to be able to orient themselves. The answer they were given was that the questions raised at the meeting would be sent seven days in advance or at least 24 hours in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So that is the beginning of March 1999. And an assessment of cooperation with the mission from that time, what would that be? Or, rather, that was an assessment. I asked you what was the assessment of the attitude and cooperation with the mission in March. I thought you were making an assertion yourself.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Cooperation with the mission at the beginning of March and end of February was as they stated here; it was very satisfactory and they expressed satisfaction with the level of cooperation and that it was always aimed at improving relations between the army of Yugoslavia and the OSCE representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We have another document here which relates to the 9th of March. Once again Kacanik and in-depth security of the border being provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Those last documents are obviously documents that should have been provided in copy form already, even if not translated. May we be sure to have them copied immediately so that we can take them away when Court rises?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll ask the court deputy to see to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mention is made here of the fact that a vehicle had run up against a mine and three men were injured. It is the 9th of March that I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it in front of me. Yes, I see that. It says at 1200 hours the Siptar terrorist forces opened fire on units of the combat group of the 4 -- 243 in the region of the village of Rezance [phoen] in Kacanik, which was engaged in providing in-depth security of the state border. A vehicle BRDM-2 from the sabotage company of the 243 Motorised Brigade encountered a PT mine and on the occasion three persons were injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And now just briefly, one more document, dated January 1999, the 4th of January, 1999. We'll just take a look at point 3. It says, during the day of the 4th of January OSCE mission team for verification in Kosovo and Metohija, led by General Maisonneuve and accompanied by the leader of the Pristina Corps team, visited companies in the region of Lapusnik, Voljak [phoen], and Dulje.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My company was Dulje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We have Dulje. Anyway, on the 4th of January, that is to say 11 days prior to the events in Racak where it is alleged that you were involved, it says that the verification of the manpower, strength and materiel was checked and representatives of the OSCE expressed satisfaction for having been allowed to tour the deployment the mixed companies in the region. So there were no comments or remarks or complaints there.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And why were they there?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there on the basis of an agreement regulating the fact that these three companies in Kosovo and Metohija were deployed. One was mine at the Dulje section, and then going on to Suva Reka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So these are the original documents, original reports. And I'd like to tender them into evidence, or at least marked for identification until we await the translations. There is a total of five reports, a set of five, and we have looked through them and quoted passages from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am just verifying whether or not these are in fact documents that were dealt with by Delic and D300, tab 449, and I've got the tab references, so perhaps when I verify that I can assist Your Honour further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Higgins, yes. In the meantime, we'll mark them for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in tab 32, we have another order by you. Can you find that? No, I'm sorry, this is an order of the command of the Pristina Corps, tab 32.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it relate to?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a command of the Pristina Corps applying to the rules of the international law of war, and it says: "In order to take measures to respect the provisions of the international law of war, the provisions the Geneva Conventions and the basic tenets of humanity, and to prevent any violation of these, I hereby order."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. We don't have to read it all. What do you consider should be highlighted here? We have an order towards persons, towards prisoners of war, the procedure and conduct towards the civilian population, and so on and so forth. All that is set out in that particular order.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is quite simply an order which explains in detail how soldiers should react in the -- in different situations. And I'd particularly like to draw your attention to the fact that following is prohibited: All forms of killing, torture, or inhumane behaviour, the taking of hostages, pronouncing sentences without prior trial by a regularly established court. "The wounded are to be given the required medical assistance." There is a ban on any taking of reprisals against POWs, wounded persons, or civilians. So it is an order which is a caution to all commanders that they must be humane in their conduct of prisoners of war whether they were direct participants against the army or whether they were engaged in a criminal act.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tab 33 is a brief report compiled by you which relates to the situation, the activities of the unit, the morale levels. Do we need to comment on that in particular?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have nothing special to add, but what is characteristic in this report is that a soldier was lightly wounded and that a vehicle was damaged at 1050 hours. All the rest is the sort of thing that you would write in a regular report going to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender that into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And that brings us to tab 34, which is an order by Vladimir Lazarevic, your superior, sent to you, and relates to the events around the village of Raka on the 5th of May.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the knowledge gained after an interview with some captured Albanian.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A man by the name of Hetem Fazli was captured during the 5th of May, and during the interview that was conducted they learnt that the said person was responsible for maintaining courier ties between the KLA staff for Kacanik and the central office of the DSK in Urosevac and that he carried out his tasks pursuant to orders from a commander called Hajrush Kurtaj, the deputy Staff Commander. In addition to this, in the town of Urosevac itself Hetem observed the positions and deployment of the units of the army of Yugoslavia and MUP, and with the information he had collected, he informed Kurtaj of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. It says here at the end of that paragraph that in the village -- it says in Seljim [phoen] -- in the villages there were 20 terrorists, armed terrorists in the sector of the villages of Kovacevac, Nika, Bicevac, and Dubrava; 50 armed terrorists.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's this area here: Kovacevac, Nika, Bicevac, and Dubrava. We discussed this area, so it was in that area that there were about 50 armed terrorists. The corps commander says: "I hereby order ..." having cautioned of the situation, he received intelligence from the security organs, and on the basis of the people detained and he orders that a plan of action should be devised to destroy the terrorists in the area of responsibility or, rather, these terrorists, and we're going to see in the other documents how far we have come with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But it is an order from the corps commander to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender that into evidence as well, tab 34.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 35 we have another document of the Supreme Command Staff. This is an order which reached the level of company commanders. "All commanders, unit commanders and other superior officers must undertake all measures in their units to ensure that every individual unit member adheres to the principles, rules and regulations of the international laws of war and conduct combat operations and beyond them." And in the next point, it says: "Any individual, whether military personnel or civilian, who violates or orders, incites, assists or participates in the violation of the principles, rules and regulations of the international laws of war shall be held personally responsible for that violation. Ignorance of the provisions of the rules and regulations of the international laws of war shall not exclude the liability of those who violate these provisions."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. It goes on to mention commanders, unit commanders, and other superior officers who must undertake necessary measures to prevent, and so on. And what does say in point 4?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that: "Any military officer who knows that there have been violations of the principles, rules and regulations of the international laws of war and does not initiate disciplinary or criminal proceedings shall be held personally responsible." It obliges every commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So if he finds out and fails to take steps to prosecute the violation. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May tab 33 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: There is also an appendix here pertaining to violations of the rules of international --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I must I say find this tedious. I hope you can bring this exercise of the orders to a swift end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In particular, this tab was tendered as tab 7 of D289, but I'm not sure it was admitted at that time. Proceed swiftly, Mr. Milosevic.
