utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of May, in tab 36, you issued a command order -- a combat order.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What can we see in this combat order in connection with the situation you described and the conditions under which your unit was acting?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It shows that during the day on several occasions the terrorists opened fire from artillery weapons in the area of deployment with 122-millimetre howitzer in the Blace and Dulje area. Until nightfall, NATO aviation, with two A10 planes, reconnoitred the area of defence of the brigade intensively, and there was enemy firing from the airspace. At 1730, 1751 fire was opened in the area Sojevo, Staro Selo. That's east of Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Staro Selo is mentioned in the parts of the indictment I quoted to you.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The people were being moved out of there. This shows that the civilians who were on the way back were being fired upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify one point. Are we looking at the same report? This one is of the 11th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says here intensive reconnaissance. At 1237, with three projectiles on the area of trig point 868 and elevation 852; at 1317 hours, with four projectiles on -- in the area of trig point 868, and so on. Is this what you are quoting?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what the effects of the bombing were on the villages in these areas?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had certain losses. In total, we had 16 losses throughout the time of the aggression. There were 88 recoverable losses and a certain number of unrecoverable ones. And there were also civilians wounded or killed. Ten or 11 were killed, mostly in the village of Sojevo, east of Urosevac, and south of Urosevac around the villages of Raka and Kamena Glava. This is where the firing was most intensive, and outside the area of the battalion of the division we had decoys to attract the fire from the planes in order to protect the combat disposition of the units, thereby protecting ourselves and the state and the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender this document into evidence, Mr. Robinson, tab 36.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 37 is a daily combat report of the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is daily combat report sent to the corps command, saying that at 0700 hours bombing started and lasted. The firing was against the Car Uros barracks and around the town of Urosevac with about 20 projectiles of different times. The enemy aviation also fired on the Stimlje-Dulje route in the Partizanski Grob sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say in 2.1 that: "In the sector of the village of Raka, numerous documents of the Siptar terrorist forces were found ..."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the MUP. These documents show that the Siptar terrorist forces are connected with the OSCE and the NATO forces for whom they have been gathering intelligence. The documents also show specific tasks of the Siptar terrorists during their preparation and carrying out of the aggression against the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's stay with this for a moment. How can you see this from these documents? I'm especially interested in what is mentioned here in this original document of the 15th of May. It says these documents show that the Siptar terrorist forces are connected with OSCE and the NATO forces for whom they have been collecting intelligence. How could this be seen?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, in the village of Raka, the complete documentation about the OSCE was found, and they had been there in Kosovo as verifiers. In view of our agreement, they had the complete documentation of my brigade. They had data on all our equipment and vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All this information that you provided to the OSCE was found with the Siptar terrorists?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those that were provided under the Vienna Convention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who do you think would have given it to them?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the verifiers who had the right not only to count the tanks but also to note the registration numbers of the engines and the various parts. This was an order that came from the corps and that was carried out in the brigades. This information was available to them. Furthermore --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The data was available to the verifiers?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they remained. The data remained in the village of Raka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you found this in the possession of the terrorists?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the KLA. The KLA also had maps which they communicated to NATO, showing where the army was positioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This is clear now. You've explained the connection. At the end here there's mention of reconnaissance of Dubrava, Gajre, Kovacevac. Is this the area where you said the 167th Brigade was active?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And if you noticed in the previous order from the corps command, we are ordered to conduct constant reconnaissance in that area and we were constantly collecting information with a view to observing them and taking action to destroy the terrorist gangs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender tab 37 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 38 there is your interim combat report.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an interim combat report. It was sent to the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, let's skip over the activities of NATO aircraft who fired projectiles of various kinds, but in the second paragraph it says on the 14th of May, 1999, Siptar terrorist forces opened infantry fire --

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sector of Djurdjev Do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says Kacanicka Klisura.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's here, on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What does it go on to say?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fire was opened in the morning in Djurdjev Do village, a territory inspection patrol from Combat Group 21 of the Nis Corps. That's a unit which was under my command for in-depth securing. It broke up a Siptar terrorist group. Three KLA members were liquidated in the clash. Two STS members were pulled out, and the third was not due to heavy enemy fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it mentions enemy casualties, three.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it confirms what was stated above. This shows that we were under constant attack during the aggression by terrorists in the brigade area and especially in the border belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In answer to previous questions, you explained that they got killed in clashes like these; when attacking our forces and when our forces returned fire.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so, because as you can see, Djurdjev Do lies behind the combat disposition of the battalion and Combat Group 21, and this attack came not from the border but from the north towards the south. It was an attack from the rear on the positions of this combat group which were securing the state border. And in this case, it was the Djeneral Jankovic pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says here that the patrol dispersed a terrorist group. In military terminology, to disperse a group, what does that imply?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To destroy is easier to explain. It means that it no longer exists, or most of it no longer exists, whereas to disperse means that a part of it only was destroyed and a part managed to pull out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this document be admitted into evidence from tab 38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 39 you have a daily combat report. It's a report of yours. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. These reports were sent on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We won't quote from it extensively, but in the middle of point 2.1, it says: "... during the reconnaissance of the zone Adam Mala - the village of Djurdjev Do, and on this occasion soldier Novica Stanojevic from the BG group was slightly wounded."

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This soldier was wounded due to terrorist activity. While he was being assisted, the terrorists approached and stole this weapon but we recovered it in the next attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Here again you have a soldier who was wounded in mid-May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Milosevic, by today. You have already utilised twice the time that you estimated for your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best, Mr. Robinson. That was tab 39. To speed up, I tender tab 39 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tab 40 says 3rd Army Command. The 3rd Army command is writing to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It mentions criminal activities and other negative instances in 3rd Army units. So this is about criminal activity in 3rd Army units.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How many men did the 3rd Army number on the 21st of May, 1999?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Full mobilisation had been carried out; it was about 170.000 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the 3rd Army had 170.000 men. This document describes characteristic instances over a month. It refers to April.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And there are one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight; eight instances.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About which the army command has information. This is only a tiny fraction of the number of men in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So what is this about?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you can see, even the smallest incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The first is the theft of a car.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to mention the name because we don't know whether the person was convicted or acquitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We won't mention any names, but again there's mention of a car theft, theft of money.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this refers to the entire 3rd Army, not just in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Consisting of several thousand men.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows that there was actually exemplary discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But the whole army was informed of this, all 170.000 men.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was sent to all units. Information was passed on in order to stop others making the same mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It goes on to say that these examples show that there are failings in the command system.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you are being asked to slow down by the interpreter. We can see the penultimate paragraph and we have the point. Please move to the next order.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I suppose you've admitted this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tab 41 contains a regular combat report of yours.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a regular combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the 22nd of May, 1999, you have active Siptar terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Enemy aviation is flying over the area of responsibility of the brigade constantly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We'll cover that.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Targeting all these features.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say in the area of hamlets Ornica and Djurdjev Do --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic is reading very fast without saying exactly where from.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Djurdjev Do, two members of the Siptar terrorist unit were killed when they walked into a minefield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 41 is hereby tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Another combat report, dated the 28th of May, is under tab 42.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "On the 27th of May, 1999, in the afternoon hours and during the night, enemy aircraft launched intensive attacks on the brigade's zone of responsibility. Around 50 missiles of various kinds were fired, and there was fire from cannons as well. The aircrafts used in the attack were F-16, F-18, and A-10."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say where. Biba village, mentioned in the indictment, Sojevo village --

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The agricultural air field, the bogus position near Raka, the Silkapor factory sector --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Which is your command post, et cetera. What can we see from this? Which areas in your brigade zone were bombed?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mainly where our positions were located, as well as our commands, our combat vehicles, with the aim of finding and destroying them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in these areas, is it also the location of various villages mentioned?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those villages were never completely abandoned. 30 to 50 per cent of the population always remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it never happens that everybody flees.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 50 per cent of the population usually stays, and when an attack happens in their vicinity, an airstrike, those people run to woods, to neighbouring villages, or to Urosevac, or go to stay with their families across the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tender 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 43 you see another regular combat report. It deals with NATO airstrikes. It's already the beginning of June 1999. In the area of Banjica village an ambush by Siptar terrorists, three members of the 243rd Brigade wounded.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So all the time, continuously, you refer to activities of Siptar terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. At this juncture, which we mentioned several times, in the area of Urosevac towards Doganovici, Vata, Slatina, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Those are the same places quoted in paragraphs I cited to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 44, we have an interim combat report dated 4th June. An ambush with fire opened from hand-held launchers and automatic rifles by Siptar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we admit that. Move to the next one.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: 45, an interim combat report. The 5th of June, again an attack, an ambush by Siptar terrorist forces in early June.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: One of your soldiers were -- was killed.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Milan Milenkovic. Medical assistance was given to him but, unfortunately, he succumbed to his wounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, we had a witness here, Florim Krasniqi from Mirosavlje village. It's one of the villages mentioned in the indictment. He stated that on the 4th of April he had seen military vehicles located near Sovtovic village, shelling Orahovici and Slatari villages, killing four persons in Slatari and wounding five. Are these allegations accurate?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He says he heard it. He couldn't have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No. It's in transcript 4447. He testified on 7th May, 2002. He says he had seen military vehicles near Sovtovic village, shelling, and killing four persons in Slatari and wounding five.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I emphasised earlier, these were positions where units were deployed. The units could not target each other because they would be killing their own men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I asked you whether this testimony is accurate.

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This witness also said that on the 5th of April Serb forces opened fire from tanks at Pojatiste. So did you or didn't you fire from tanks at Pojatiste on the 5th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not, nor were we able to because our units were just outside Pojatiste. We did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this is not correct?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's on the same page of the transcript. Now, on 4485, he says that he saw on the 7th of April houses burning in Sojevo and Kamena Glava and he heard that seven people were killed on that occasion. What do you know about this incident? 7th of April, 1999 houses burning in Sojevo and Kamena Glava, seven people killed?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of the deaths of these people. If they had happened, I would have heard about it. They could have been in areas hit by NATO aviations. More than seven houses were hit in Sojevo and Kamena Glava, but in many other places, and there were daily airstrikes from Varos Selo to the air field Sojevo via Kamena Glava, this axis. The juncture -- junction leading to Urosevac and Pristina further on. There was an armoured battalion in the area. It was natural, with so many airstrikes, that some buildings would be hit, and we indeed saw some houses burning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We -- I'm stopping at 1.43. There's another trial, and I'll not be resuming tomorrow with your examination in chief. You have taken more than twice the time estimated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have several more questions. I can't understand that I could not be given the possibility to ask them. This is a very important witness, Mr. Robinson, a commander of a brigade covering a very large area, who can give us examples of everything that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have two minutes -- three minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot manage in two minutes. I need at least half an hour to finish examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Bajram Bucaliu, a Prosecution witness from Staro Selo, Urosevac municipality, claims that on the 2nd of April, 1999 the Serb army surrounded Staro Selo. Do you know anything about this? Was this village surrounded?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. It's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In his testimony he states that on the 3rd of April the army searched houses. Do you know why army searched houses?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army never searched any houses. That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is the claim of this witness correct that on the 5th of April paramilitaries arrived at his village, blocking exits from the village?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no paramilitary forces in the zone of responsibility of my brigade, including this village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He claims that on the 14th of April, three villagers were killed after which villagers started to flee towards Urosevac. What do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He says that on the 15th of April he came to the railway station in Urosevac and there were 4 to 5.000 people there, that about 25.000 people went towards the border by train, that the train was escorted by the police to the Macedonian border when the Macedonian authorities turned them back to Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What do you know about this large number of refugees in Urosevac? Why would the police escort this convoy to the border, especially 25.000 people travelling by train?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the Urosevac railway station could never take that amount of people. Such a mass of people never existed there. For 25.000 people, it would take 150 -- rather, no, 250 rail cars. What kind of train could take that number of people? So it's an obvious lie. This train usually had three to four rail cars and there were three or four trains per day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is this claim a possibility at all?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's absurd. It's completely impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I won't go through the paragraphs referring to the confiscation of documents and personal identification papers. What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never confiscated anybody's IDs. It was not our job and we were never located on roads or border crossings or anywhere where you could do that kind of thing. It was not within our purview to respect anybody's identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just one more thing. Tab 46. That's the last document. What is it?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the rule of conduct for soldiers. It was issued before the war and every soldier had it on him. It's a rule that every soldier had to study.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I am asking you very specifically: Did every soldier in your brigade have this rule?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody had a copy, a laminated version that had to be carried in a pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It is claimed in paragraph 55 that there was deliberate and systematic expulsion of hundreds of thousands of Albanians. Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: KRSMAN JELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of any such plan and there was no organisation made to expel anybody in my zone of responsibility or anywhere else in Kosovo and Metohija, as far as I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 3. We are going to adjourn now and tomorrow Mr. Nice will commence his cross-examination. Tab 46 is admitted. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
